Article Title: India vs Sri Lanka 2nd Test: With Rishabh Pant beside him, Dhruv Jurel finds his own voice
Article Text:
Dhruv Jurel (AFP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dhruv Jurel marked his century on Day Two of the second Test with a salute, before pointing to the tattoo on his biceps, ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’ — former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri’s tribute to India’s soldiers and farmers during the 1965 Indo-Pak war.Jurel is the son of Kargil War veteran Nem Singh Jurel, a retired Indian Army havaldar.“My grandfather was a farmer and my father was a soldier. Those are my roots and I don’t want to forget them. That salute was for them,” Jurel said after his sparkling ton.The Uttar Pradesh wicketkeeper-batter, whose Instagram bio reads ‘Mamba Mentality’ in reference to Kobe Bryant’s philosophy, has strengthened his claim to the No. 6 Test spot despite competition from Sarfaraz Khan.Before the Sri Lanka series, Jurel had gone eight innings without a 50-plus score, with questions being raised over his game against spin. He responded with 51 in the first Test and followed it with his second Test hundred, taking his series tally to 173 runs at an average of 86.5.The Indian team management has backed Jurel as a specialist middle-order batter even when he is not required to keep wickets.“Jurel will serve Indian cricket for a long time. His form for India ‘A’ in Sri Lanka in July, where he scored 208 runs in two matches at 104, including a century, helped him,” a key decision-maker in Indian cricket told TOI.Before the Colombo Test, Cheteshwar Pujara had also urged India to persist with Jurel at No. 6.“I don’t think Jurel should be excluded. He batted brilliantly in the first innings of the first Test. India should stick with him,” Pujara said.Jurel shared a 112-run stand for the seventh wicket with Rishabh Pant and said he often turns to him for advice.“We all know what Pant has done for India in Australia and England. Whenever he is batting with me, I ask him what I should do in a situation,” Jurel said, dedicating his hundred to his parents.He added that while Pant’s attacking style is unique, he prefers to stick to his own methods.“I can’t play like Pant. My plan is to identify which bowler to attack and which spell to play out. Since both of us are wicketkeepers and middle-order batters, I always ask him for advice,” he said.Jurel reached 99 off 123 balls before taking a risky single off Asitha Fernando to complete his hundred.“Till 99, I was getting runs, but then Asitha started bowling good lengths and Sri Lanka fielded well. When I punched it over the bowler’s head, I thought there was a gap. Then I saw the fielder coming close and thought, ‘Oh, what have I done?’” he said.Jurel also thanked Mohammed Siraj, who blocked 29 balls to help him reach the milestone.“Siraj celebrates more than me. The good thing was his defence was solid.”
Article Summary: Dhruv Jurel scores century in second Test against Sri Lanka. Uttar Pradesh wicketkeeper-batter has strengthened his claim to the No. 6 Test spot. He had gone eight innings without a 50-plus score, with questions raised over his game against spin.

Article Title: BWF World Championships: Treesa-Gayatri's medal, Ayush's shock and PV Sindhu's fight define a tournament to remember
Article Text:
Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand (Image credit: BAI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: When the curtain came down on the BWF World Championships at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, Indian badminton found itself standing at a defining intersection of pride, introspection and structural redemption.Seventeen years after India last hosted the prestigious global showpiece in Hyderabad, the Delhi edition delivered an emphatic statement both on and off the court.Just seven months earlier, the venue had been mired in embarrassment during the India Open Super 750, a tournament marred by stray animal intrusions, monkey sightings, bird droppings and widespread player discontent.Fast forward to August, and a Rs 20 crore infrastructure overhaul featuring advanced anti-perch roof gels, enhanced climate control and meticulous operational execution turned the arena into a world-class colosseum.The turnaround was so comprehensive that the Capital has now emerged as a prime contender to host the 2028 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals.On the court, the week belonged unreservedly to Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, whose stirring campaign culminated in a historic women’s doubles bronze medal.Ranked world No. 39 and unseeded, the duo ended a 15-year medal drought in the discipline — dating back to Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa’s bronze in London in 2011 — while keeping intact India’s proud streak of securing at least one podium finish at every World Championships since 2011.Treesa and Gayatri’s giantkilling run was built on relentless aggression and tactical discipline.They stunned Japanese seventh seeds Rin Iwanaga and Kie Nakanishi in the pre-quarters before mounting a sensational comeback from a game down to conquer Chinese fourth seeds Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian in the quarterfinals.Although they eventually fell to the world No. 1 Chinese pair of Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning in an electric semifinal, their fearless baseline shot making and sharp net play won over the home fans.“If you see the whole week, it has been amazing. We created big upsets, played great matches and have so many positives to take away,” said Treesa.Chief national coach Pullela Gopichand said, “Treesa and Gayatri showed extraordinary heart. Pushing top-five pairs of the world in highpressure situations proves the strides our doubles programme has made.”While doubles provided the silverware, the men’s singles draw produced the tournament’s biggest shock courtesy 21-year-old Ayush Shetty.The lanky debutant scripted history on opening day by dethroning defending champion and world No. 1 Shi Yu Qi of China.Ayush followed it up with a clinical 26-minute demolition of Sri Lanka’s Dumin­du Abeywickrama before bowing out to Indonesia’s Alwi Farhan in the prequarters.Ayush’s giantkilling act mirrored a wider generational shift in men’s singles.With France’s Alex Lanier capturing a historic maiden world title — the first Frenchman to do so — and Canada’s Victor Lai claiming bronze, the tournament illustrated that sustained dominance, once the hallmark of Lin Dan, Lee Chong Wei or Viktor Axelsen, has given way to fierce parity across the men’s singles draw.“There are more tournaments nowadays, and there are also more good players. The intensity in the opening round itself is already very high,” Lanier said.Lai concurred, stating: “Anyone in the top 30 can beat anyone. There are no easy matches.”For India’s established singles stars, the week was bittersweet.Former world champion PV Sindhu looked sharp in her opening rounds, dispatching Ireland’s Sophia Noble and Canada’s Wen Yu Zhang.However, her bid for a sixth Worlds medal ended in an 88-minute pre-quarterfinal marathon against third seed Wang Zhi Yi of China.In contrast, Lakshya Sen flattered to deceive.After clawing past Austria’s Collins Filimon in three games, the world No. 14 suffered a shock second-round exit against USA’s world No. 92 Garret Tan.“Lakshya lost to a very ordinary player, and there is no excuse for this performance. He was too passive and allowed the opponent to dictate,” former chief national coach Vimal Kumar said.Elsewhere in the Indian camp, fifth seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty reached the quarterfinals before going down to eventual champions Liang Wei Keng and Wang Chang of China.Debutant Unnati Hooda showed immense grit, beating Thet Htar Thuzar in the opening round before missing two match points in a 21-23 decider against 13th seed Michelle Li.Mixed doubles pair Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto reached the pre-quarters, while men’s doubles duo MR Arjun-Hariharan Amsakarunan and women’s doubles combination Kavipriya Selvam-Simran Singhi tallied opening-round wins.
Article Summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand claim women's doubles bronze medal. 21-year- old Ayush Shetty stuns world No. 1 Shi Yu Qi in men's singles. Alex Lanier and Victor Lai claim men's and women's bronze respectively.

Article Title: Hockey World Cup: Argentina dash India’s slim semifinal hopes
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Thirty-six seconds. That was all it took for India’s threadbare hope of reaching the FIH World Cup semifinals to disappear.At the Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, Netherlands, Argentina exposed India’s defensive frailties and ended Harmanpreet Singh and his men’s semifinal aspirations with a 5-3 win in their final Stage 2 match on Monday.Saturday’s 1-3 defeat to cohosts Netherlands had all but extinguished India’s hopes of a podium finish. Argentina, however, drove the final nail into the coffin.Lacklustre defending, poor marking and possession that produced little end product summed up India’s evening. For all their control of the ball, they struggled to keep Argentina’s attackers at bay.The only consolation was that two of India’s three goals came from open play. But seven penalty corners went begging, a statistic that once again underlined their struggles.Barely had India settled into the contest when Joaquin Toscani punished a defensive error. Jarmanpreet Singh failed to intercept a ball across the goalmouth and Toscani made no mistake, firing Argentina ahead.Argentina kept the pressure on and doubled their advantage. Nicolas della Torre converted the ir second penalty corner in the sixth minute, exposing another lapse in India’s defensive organisation. Sukhjeet Singh gave India a lifeline in the 10th minute, finishing from close range.India had opportunities to draw level in the second quarter but failed to take them.Argentina restored their two-goal advantage when Tomas Domene’s 33rd minute reverse hit beat goalkeeper HS Mohith.Domene then completed his brace in the 45th minute, converting a penalty stroke. Lucas Toscani added Argentina’s fifth, leaving Indian shoulders sagging.Sukhjeet pulled one back in the 58th minute before Hardil Singh reduced the margin further a minute later.India will now play Belgium in the 7-8 classification match.
Article Summary: Argentina exposed India's defensive frailties and ended Harmanpreet Singh and his men's semifinal aspirations with a 5-3 win in their final Stage 2 match on Monday. Saturday’s 1-3 defeat to cohosts Netherlands had all but extinguished India's hopes of a podium finish.

Article Title: Durand Cup triumph a whiff of redemption for Edmund and Habas
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: When people’s paths cross, sometimes it comes with the whiff of a road movie evolving and eventually moving their journey towards its point of redemption with a profound sense of inevitability.For Edmund Lalrindika and Antonio Lopez Habas — the two main characters of East Bengal FC’s audacious dismantling of Mohun Bagan SG on their way to winning the Durand Cup here on Sunday, their journeys perhaps wield a symbolism with much depth and emotional nuance. They are about returning to the battle front not only to survive a seemingly insurmountable ordeal but completing an unfinished business with a beguiling element of defiance.Six years ago it was at the very Salt Lake Stadium, Edmund saw his journey suffer an unexpected setback. Five days after joining an Alejandro Menendez’s East Bengal on a short-term loan deal from Bengaluru FC, the Mizo youngster made debut in the first-leg I-League derby in the 2019-2020 season, coming off the bench to provide an assist for Macros Jimenez’s goal in a match which Mohun Bagan eventually won 2-1. It was the penultimate I-League derby between the two traditional rivals before their foray into the Indian Super League which was coronated as the country’s top-tier league. Edmund’s stay in the match was merely 14-minute long as it was cut short with a serious injury, forcing him to leave the field and return to the BFC fold.Two years later, another spine injury put a serious question mark over his future, with his doctors having advised to stay away from football. But Edmund defied the odds with his customary grit and a year after joining Inter Kashi, he found in Habas a catalyst he had been waiting to process his rebirth with a structure of meaning.If Edmund’s journey to self-realization was marinated in suffering, the one for Habas had a smidge of rejection. Having returned to take charge of Mohun Bagan Super Giant midway in the 2023-2024 season and guided them to the ISL Winners’ Shield, the veteran Spanish coach didn’t find any backers from the team management to continue and took the plunge into the second tier of Indian club football with Inter Kashi.Edmund — already becoming the first player from I-League to earn a call-up in the senior national team since ISL’s promotion to the top league — welcomed the Spaniard to the newly-formed team with a late winner, helping Inter Kashi edge past SC Bengaluru at Kalyani stadium on Nov 24 in 2024. Habas went on to transform his precious pupil from a winger to an attacker, often employing him as a False 9 position. The result was dazzling for the duo and devastating for the rivals. As Inter Kashi eventually won the I-League and earned their promotion to ISL, Edmund made his choice — returning to East Bengal and completing a mission he had left unfinished.When Habas left his position as Inter Kashi coach three matches before the end of the 2025-2026 season and returned to Spain amid uncertainty over ISL’s future, East Bengal too were forced to search for a new beginning, days after winning the ISL. Coach Oscar Bruzon had already made his intention of leaving clear to everyone and investor Emami Group was unwilling to pump in money in the red-and-gold project.The club officials had to step in and when Habas received a call from them to take reins of the new ISL champions, he was always game for a homecoming with a difference.As fate would have it, Edmund reunited with his mentor and the duo created quite a buzz on Sunday.“I’ve not won the Durand Cup in my career. So, it’s a special one,” Habas told reporters after the final.“Hopefully, it’s just the start of a new journey and more trophies will follow,” a beaming Edmund remarked.
Article Summary: Edmund Lalrindika and Antonio Lopez Habas are the two main characters of East Bengal FC’s audacious dismantling of Mohun Bagan SG on their way to winning the Durand Cup here on Sunday. Their journeys perhaps wield a symbolism with much depth and emotional nuance. They are about returning to the battle front not only to survive a seemingly insurmountable ordeal but completing an unfinished business.

Article Title: Premier League Sunday drama: Man City, Liverpool rescue points as Brighton thrash Villa
Article Text:
Manchester City's Josko Gvardiol (24) celebrates with teammates after scoring his side's second goal. (AP Photo)

Maresca gets dream City start

Szoboszlai saves Liverpool at Newcastle

Brighton tear Villa apart

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The first Sunday of the new Premier League season delivered late drama, stirring comebacks and a statement win, with Manchester City and Liverpool both scoring deep into stoppage time while Brighton produced a ruthless 4-0 demolition of Aston Villa.For Enzo Maresca, it was the perfect start to life as Manchester City manager. City scored twice in the final 10 minutes to overturn Bournemouth and seal a 2-1 victory, while Liverpool needed a ninth-minute stoppage-time penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to snatch a 2-2 draw at Newcastle.Maresca, who replaced Pep Guardiola, had endured a difficult first competitive outing when City lost 0-3 to Arsenal in the Community Shield last weekend. His Premier League debut looked set to end in disappointment after Bournemouth took the lead, but City found another gear late on.Marc Guehi equalised in the 84th minute with a header from a corner before Josko Gvardiol completed the turnaround in the first minute of added time. The goal was initially ruled out for offside but was awarded after a video review.Maresca punched the air before heading onto the pitch after the final whistle to embrace his players.“It is the perfect day, to be honest,” Maresca said. “I was very pleased when the game started to see the banner on the other side. And I was pleased because we give them the joy of the three points. “It was quite emotional and the perfect day.”The Italian had earlier surprised by deploying Guehi, a centre-back, as a holding midfielder. The decision looked questionable initially but Guehi grew into the role. Erling Haaland , meanwhile, endured a frustrating afternoon and failed to score in a Premier League season opener for the first time since joining City in 2022.Liverpool also needed a dramatic late intervention to avoid defeat at Newcastle in a match that featured tributes to former England and Newcastle and Liverpool star Kevin Keegan, who died last month aged 75.Anthony Elanga gave Newcastle the lead in the fifth minute before Cody Gakpo equalised early in the second half. Joe Willock restored Newcastle’s advantage just moments after coming off the bench, setting up a frantic finale.Liverpool were handed a lifeline when debutant Victor Munoz was fouled inside the area. After a video review lasting three-and-a-half minutes, the penalty was confirmed, allowing Szoboszlai to step up and smash an unstoppable effort into the top corner in the ninth minute of stoppage time.“I really hit it good,” the Hungary captain said. “I love the pressure.”The game also saw Alexander Isak endure a hostile reception from Newcastle supporters following his move away from the club.Brighton made the biggest statement of the day, scoring four times inside the opening 31 minutes to crush Aston Villa 4-0.Brighton’s sharpness was evident after their midweek European qualifying action, while Villa struggled badly after a difficult offseason. Their misery increased when Joao Gomes was sent off in the 40th minute for kicking out at Georginio Rutter.Villa were unable to recover, although Brighton failed to add to their tally after the dismissal.The day ended on a sombre note when a 72-year-old Brighton supporter died after falling ill while leaving the Amex Stadium following the victory.Despite efforts from emergency services and club staff, the supporter could not be saved. Brighton chief executive Paul Barber said: “we are all shocked and saddened by the loss of one of our supporters.”
Article Summary: Manchester City beat Bournemouth 2-1 on Enzo Maresca's Premier League debut. City scored twice in the final 10 minutes to seal victory. Liverpool needed a ninth-minute stoppage-time penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to snatch a 2-2 draw at Newcastle. Brighton produced a ruthless 4-0 demolition of Aston Villa.

Article Title: 'Let him leave once and for all': Atletico asks Julian Alvarez to 'not go near fans' as transfer saga spills
Article Text:
Julian Alvarez

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Was the red card for Robin Le Normand justified? Yes, it was a clear foul No, it was too harsh 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Giuliano Simeone scored a late equaliser as Atletico Madrid came back to draw 2-2 with Villarreal after playing the final stages of the match with 10 men.The late goal came after Villarreal had taken the lead from the penalty spot following Robin Le Normand's red card in the 76th minute.Le Normand was sent off for bringing down Georges Mikautadze inside the box, and Mikautadze converted the penalty to put Villarreal 2-1 ahead.Atletico responded with one final counter-attack. Alex Baena played the ball to Giuliano Simeone on the right, and the forward finished past goalkeeper Luiz Junior to earn his father Diego Simeone's side a point.The match also saw Atletico supporters turn against Julian Alvarez.The striker was booed while warming up, jeered again when his name was announced among the substitutes, and received louder whistles when he came on in the 66th minute.Some fans also chanted, "Let him leave once and for all, let him leave..." after Alvarez had said during the World Cup that he had spoken to the club about a possible transfer to "fulfil my dream". Spanish media have linked him with Barcelona.The boos continued after the final whistle as Alvarez went straight to the dressing room while the rest of the Atletico players stayed back to acknowledge the fans.After the match, Diego Simeone said the club had decided Alvarez should avoid going near the supporters."The club decided he should not go near the stands or the fans," the Atletico manager said in a press conference."It was the club's decision to keep him away and separate him, so he could go to the locker room."When asked what advice he would give Alvarez, Simeone replied: "I'm not here to give advice. I have to focus on my job, which is to give my best for Atletico Madrid. If we want to win a title, we need to stick together, have forwards, and have key forwards. We all need to work accordingly on what we need."After a goalless first half, Atletico took the lead in the 59th minute through Marc Pubill, who scored from outside the box.Villarreal equalised seven minutes later after Morten Hjulmand gave away a penalty for a foul on Tajon Buchanan, and Gerard Moreno converted the spot kick past Jan Oblak.VAR later awarded Villarreal another penalty after Le Normand's challenge on Mikautadze, which also resulted in the defender being sent off.Despite being down to 10 men, Atletico found a late equaliser through Giuliano Simeone to finish with a point.
Article Summary: Giuliano Simeone scores late equaliser as Atletico Madrid draw 2-2 with Villarreal. Robin Le Normand was sent off in the 76th minute for a foul on Georges Mikautadze. Atletico played the final stages of the match with 10 men. Match also saw Atletico supporters turn against Julian Alvarez.

Article Title: $7 million! AG.AL crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champion after landmark Paris edition
Article Text:
AG.AL crowned Esports World Cup 2026 Club Champion (Pic credit: EWC 2026)

AG.AL complete remarkable campaign

Paris delivers record numbers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

AG.AL were crowned Esports World Cup 2026 club champions after a dramatic final weekend in Paris, securing the $7 million (~INR 66.9 crore) top prize following seven weeks of record-breaking esports action featuring more than 2,000 players, 200 Clubs and 25 tournaments across 24 games.AG.AL finished on 5,300 points, edging two-time defending champions Team Falcons, who ended runners-up with 4,600 points. Team Vitality finished third with 3,300 points, followed by Natus Vincere (2,950) and Team Liquid (2,700).The club championship went down to the wire, with AG.AL completing their campaign through Gwendal “Gwen” Duparc's victory in the inaugural Trackmania tournament. The Frenchman delivered under pressure to win the tournament and secure the club championship for AG.AL.Falcons had entered the Trackmania playoffs at the top of the overall standings, but Carl-Antoni “Carl Jr.” Cloutier's quarterfinal exit opened the door for AG.AL. Gwen then dominated the final, securing the $130,000 (~INR 1.2 crore) tournament prize and, more importantly, the club championship.AG.AL's title-winning campaign also featured a first-place finish in Tekken 8, second-place finishes in Chess, Free Fire and the Honor of Kings World Cup, and a third-place finish in Teamfight Tactics.“When we began expanding AG.AL globally in 2024, the same year the Esports World Cup launched, we set out to build a Club capable of succeeding across games, regions and cultures. This title shows how far that vision has come,” said Eddy Chen, COO at AG.AL.“Our journey in Paris reflected the strength of the entire organization, from M. Zubair’s breakthrough in TEKKEN 8 and our deep runs across multiple titles to Gwen delivering the decisive Trackmania victory under extraordinary pressure. But this trophy belongs equally to every player, coach and staff member whose dedication brought us here.”The Paris edition also produced several memorable individual performances. France's Caliste “Caliste” Henry-Hennebert led Karmine Corp to the League of Legends Grand Final in front of a home crowd, while 15-year-old Chilean Jaime “Craime” Bustos became the youngest Esports World Cup champion after defeating two EVO champions.AG.AL's Khawaja “M. Zubair” also captured the Tekken 8 title, while Rocket League star Samy “dralii” Hajji became the first three-time Esports World Cup champion. Grandmaster Magnus Carlsen successfully defended his Chess title without losing a game.The 2026 edition set new benchmarks for the Esports World Cup, with the event reaching 850 million viewers and generating 440 million hours watched — increases of 13% and 26%, respectively, year-on-year. Peak viewership reached 4.3 million during the League of Legends tournament.The event was distributed globally through more than 100 broadcast and OTT partners in 47 languages, with 5,000 creators and co-streamers supporting its coverage.In another major milestone, 175,000 tickets were sold for esports competitions, a 94% increase from 2025. Total visits across competition venues, Fan Fest and city activations exceeded two million during the seven-week event.“We are proud of what the Esports World Cup has achieved in Paris and of its continued international growth,” said His Royal Highness Prince Faisal bin Bandar bin Sultan al Saud, Chairman of the Executive Committee of the Esports Foundation.“Bringing the EWC to a global audience beyond Saudi Arabia marks an important milestone in its journey and reflects the growing recognition of esports as a global industry, connecting communities, cultures and audiences around the world.”Paris was the first city outside Riyadh to host the Esports World Cup. More than 22,600 campaign placements across the capital reached 94% of Parisians, while the final weekend's Counter-Strike tournament was staged at the 20,000-seat Accor Arena.The event followed a year-long competitive journey involving more than 1.5 million players across 330 Road to EWC events.“Our ambition has always been bigger than a single event: to grow esports and establish it as a leading global sport,” said Ralf Reichert, Chief Executive Officer of the Esports Foundation.The Esports World Cup will return to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in 2027.
Article Summary: AG.AL win $7 million (~INR 66.9 crore) top prize following seven weeks of record-breaking esports action. AG.AL finished on 5,300 points, edging two-time defending champions Team Falcons, who ended runners-up with 4,600 points. More than 2,000 players, 200 Clubs and 25 tournaments across 24 games.

Article Title: Rohan Bopanna hits out at Asian Games tennis-squad cuts
Article Text:
Rohan Bopanna (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: “Let sport decide, not a spreadsheet.” That was the sharp message from twotime Asian Games gold medallist Rohan Bopannaas the pruning of India’s tennis squad by the sports ministry for the Aichi-Nagoya Games triggered a fresh debate over selection policy.Bopanna backed five players who have been dropped from the 12-member list recommended by the All India Tennis Association (AITA), questioning the wisdom of deciding medal prospects before players have stepped on to the court.“If outcomes are already decided, why have qualifications at all? Why rankings?” he wrote on social media.The ministry-approved seven-member tennis contingent comprises Sumit Nagal and Dhakshineswar Suresh for men’s singles; Yuki Bhambri, N Sriram Balaji and Anirudh Chandrasekar for men’s doubles and Ankita Raina and Rutuja Bhosale for women’s doubles.There is no women’s singles representation.Importantly, the 2026 Asiad singles champions can earn an ITF quota place for the LA 2028 Games, subject to eligibility requirements. Not sending a singles specialist could hurt the nation’s Olympics chances.The omissions are Manas Dhamne, Vaishnavi Adkar, Sahaja Yamalapalli, Vaidehee Chaudhari and Prarthana Thombare.The ministry, however, has shown no inclination to revisit its decision.TOIsent a detailed questionnaire to the ministry, Sports Authority of India and TOPS division seeking a formal response to the Bopanna-led criticism. A response is awaited.
Article Summary: Rohan Bopanna criticises India's tennis squad for the Aichi-Nagoya Games. The Asian Games gold medallist has backed five players dropped from the 12-member list recommended by the All India Tennis Association. The ministry-approved seven-member tennis contingent comprises Sumit Nagal and Dhakshineswar Suresh for men’s singles.

Article Title: 'Amazing India': BWF President Khunying Patama lauds New Delhi for hosting World Championships
Article Text:
BWF President lauds Delhi’s World Championships hosting (Image: IANS)

'India made every year count'

BAI, government and SAI praised

Players' experience ‘matters more than anything’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

‘Proud of the fans in India’

‘A tournament, but a beginning’

NEW DELHI: India may have fallen short of its medal ambitions at the BWF World Championships 2026, with only a bronze in women's doubles, but the country earned high praise for its organisation and hospitality as host of the prestigious tournament after a 17-year wait.BWF President Khunying Patama Leeswadtrakul hailed India's efforts in hosting the championships in New Delhi, describing the week as a memorable experience and thanking the organisers, government authorities, volunteers, officials, sponsors and fans for their contribution.Reflecting on the tournament, Leeswadtrakul said India had waited 17 years to host the World Championships again and made the opportunity count."What a week New Delhi has given us. India waited 17 years for this moment, and India made every year count," the BWF president wrote in her message. She said the championships had received widespread praise from across the badminton community and credited the people behind the event for its success.Leeswadtrakul acknowledged the role of the Badminton Association of India (BAI), which was responsible for hosting the championships, while also praising the Government of India and the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports for their support.She also highlighted the contribution of the Sports Authority of India (SAI), particularly in delivering the tournament arena.The BWF president noted that India had built a facility capable of hosting badminton's biggest stage despite a demanding timeline.The tournament's volunteers and technical officials were also singled out for praise. Leeswadtrakul said volunteers worked for countless days while maintaining a positive spirit, while technical officials put in long hours to ensure the competition ran smoothly and professionally.She also thanked sponsors and partners for backing the championships and helping bring the event to life.The BWF president placed particular emphasis on the experience provided to players and team officials. She said athletes were offered good hotels, reliable transportation and facilities that allowed them to prepare without distractions. Players and officials, she added, had praised the courts, playing conditions and overall arrangements."That matters more than anything," Leeswadtrakul said.The BWF president also praised the local crowd, saying Indian fans demonstrated their knowledge of the sport while creating an energetic atmosphere throughout the tournament."I am proud of the fans in India, who know this sport and cheer with real knowledge. And I am proud of a country that opened its heart to the world," she wrote.For Leeswadtrakul, however, the biggest legacy of the championships extended beyond the medals and results. She highlighted the children who attended the event, saying some may have picked up a badminton racket for the first time after watching the world's best players compete."That is what a great host leaves behind. Not only a tournament, but a beginning," she said before signing off with a simple message: "Thank you, India."
Article Summary: BWF President Khunying Patama Leeswadtrakul hails India's efforts in hosting the championships in New Delhi. She describes the week as a memorable experience and thanks the organisers, government authorities, volunteers, officials, sponsors and fans for their contribution.

Article Title: Men’s Hockey World Cup: How can India qualify for the semifinals? The permutations explained

What India need to do against Argentina

NEW DELHI: India's hopes of reaching the semifinals of the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 are hanging by a thread after their second-round defeat to the Netherlands, but Argentina's 3-1 win over England has kept Craig Fulton's side mathematically alive.India suffered a 1-3 loss to the Netherlands on Saturday, leaving them bottom of Pool E with no points from their two matches. However, England's defeat to Argentina later in the day opened a narrow route to the last four.The equation is now simple in principle, although the margins are anything but: India must beat Argentina and then hope the Netherlands defeat England by a sufficiently large margin.India must beat Argentina by at least two goals in their final Pool E match on Monday.A two-goal victory would give India three points and allow them to move above Argentina on goals scored, provided the relevant goal-difference calculations remain level. A victory by more than two goals would give India the advantage on goal difference.The task, however, is easier said than done. Argentina have already beaten India twice in the FIH Pro League this year, winning 8-0 and 4-2.India therefore need not only a victory but a convincing one to keep their semifinal hopes alive.Even if India beat Argentina, their qualification will depend on the result of Netherlands vs England.The Dutch are already top of Pool E with six points and a goal difference of +4, while England and Argentina have three points each with goal differences of zero. India have zero points and a -4 goal difference after conceding seven goals and scoring three.The safest route for India is a two-goal win over Argentina combined with a three-goal victory for the Netherlands against England.For example, if India beat Argentina 3-1 and England lose 0-3 to the Netherlands, India would finish ahead of England on goal difference and eliminate Argentina. The Netherlands would top the pool with nine points, leaving India second.Some results could produce further tie-break complications. If India win 3-1 and England lose 1-3, both would have identical goals scored and conceded, meaning the field-goal tie-break could come into play.India currently have one field goal in the pool, Dilpreet Singh's strike against England, while England have three.The final-day schedule adds another twist. India play Argentina at 6:30pm IST on Monday, while England face the Netherlands at 10:30pm IST.That means England will know exactly what they need from their match against the Dutch based on India's result earlier in the evening.
Article Summary: India must beat Argentina by at least two goals in their final Pool E match on Monday. Article Title: Duleep Trophy: J&K spinner Abid Mushtaq's five-for tightens North Zone’s grip
Article Text:

East Zone in command

BENGALURU: Some spinners rely on guile and variety, others on subtle change of pace. Abid Mushtaq prefers a simpler route to success— hit the right areas, make batters play and wait for them to commit mistakes.The Jammu and Kashmir leftarm spinner was at his methodical best against West Zone on Day Two of the Duleep Trophy at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here on Monday. On a red-soil pitch he described as his “favourite”, Abid claimed a five-wicket haul to bowl West out for 187 in 65.4 overs.North Zone, who secured a 64-run first-innings lead, were 107/4 at stumps, stretching their advantage to 171 runs.Abid admitted he got “goosebumps” when he saw the red soil, a surface he has only started training on regularly over the last 3-4 three years in J&K. He made the most of the familiarity, producing a spell built on accuracy rather than elaborate variations.The 29-year-old, who was also invited to bowl in the Australian team’s nets ahead of the 2023 BorderGavaskar Trophy in India, kept attacking the stumps and forcing batters to play.Three of his five wickets — Shivalik Sharma, Ruturaj Gaikwad and Urvil Patel — came via LBWs. Gaikwad and Urvil fell within three balls of each other, leaving West reeling at 70/5 in the 28th over.“I bowled at the stumps as there was a lot of help on the wicket. I always try to land in good areas and not give away runs. I also use the crease. When it comes to bowling in red soil, I’m confident,” Abid said.His figures of 11-5-13-3 in the first session summed up his approach. He gave the batters little to work with and had already castled Prithvi Shaw on Sunday evening.Abid, who has taken 63 wickets in his last three Ranji Trophy seasons, kept varying his angle, bowling from both sides of the wicket without compromising on his discipline.Musheer Khan (31), who showed considerable patience against him, and Shams Mulani (52) briefly stemmed the collapse with a 63-run sixth-wicket partnership. But Abid returned to dismiss Tushar Deshpande (18), completing his five-for.Anshul Kamboj (2/38) and Arshdeep Singh (3/53) also contributed with the ball as North Zone tightened their grip on the quarterfinal.At the adjacent ground, Shahbaz Ahmed produced an allround performance to put East Zone firmly in control against North East Zone.Resuming on 100, the left-hander went on to make 167 as East amassed 467 in 112.5 overs. His innings built on the foundation laid by Sudip Gharami’s 146 on the opening day.Shahbaz then took 3/20 as North East were bowled out for 111, with Abhijit Sarkar returning 5/20.Forced to follow on, North East reached 7/0 from the only over possible before stumps.North Zone 251 & 107/4 in 21 overs (Ayush Badoni 39*, Abdul Samad 30; Shams Mulani 2/34, Tanush Kotian 2/22) vs West Zone 187 in 65.4 overs (Shams Mulani 52, Musheer Khan 31; Abid Mushtaq 5/39, Arshdeep Singh 3/53, Anshul Kamboj 2/38).East Zone 467 in 112.5 overs (Shahbaz Ahmed 167, Sudip Gharami 146, Kumar Kushagra 55, Anukul Roy 37; Jotin Pheiroijam 3/64, Akash Choudhary 3/102, Bishworjit Konthoujam 2/92) vs North East Zone 111 in 42.5 overs (Arpit Bhatewara 32; Abhijit Sarkar 5/20, Shahbaz Ahmed 3/20) & 7/0 in 1 over.
Article Summary: Abid Mushtaq takes five-wicket haul to bowl West out for 187 in 65.4 overs. North Zone secure 64-run first-innings lead, stretching advantage to 171 runs. Shahbaz Ahmed takes 3/20 as North East were bowled out for 111.

Article Title: India vs Sri Lanka 2nd Test: Dhruv Jurel's 115 not out, Rishabh Pant's blazing 63 power India to 503/9
Article Text:
Dhruv Jurel (AFP Photo)

It was one of the riskiest singles Dhruv Jurel would have taken in his Test career. Anxious to complete his second Test century — and first overseas hundred — after being stranded on 99 for 12 balls and made to wait by rain while on 95, Jurel punched the ball towards mid-off and sprinted for a single that just wasn’t on.The ball travelled quickly to the fielder after bouncing. But luck smiled on the 25-year-old batter. The fielder missed the direct hit and Jurel dived to complete the run and his century, which came off 171 balls and had the entire Indian dressing room applauding as they shared the tension. Mohammed Siraj celebrated wildly, giving Jurel a bear hug.Powered by Jurel’s composed and flawless unbeaten 115 off 177 balls, with nine fours and two sixes, and Rishabh Pant ’s entertaining 63 off 89 balls, with six fours and two sixes, India declared at 503 for nine. Then, they reduced Sri Lanka to 8/2 on Day Two of the second and final Test in Colombo on Monday.The hosts were clearly unhappy about being asked to bat in fading light. Yashasvi Jaiswal pulled off a brilliant diving catch at gully to send back Lahiru Udara for one off Prasidh Krishna in the second over.In the third over, the hosts suffered another blow when nightwatchman Prabath Jayasuriya was trapped LBW for two by a fast, full delivery from Manav Suthar.Jayasuriya’s agitated reaction after being dismissed reflected Sri Lanka’s unhappiness at being asked to bat so late in the evening.Kamil Mishara was batting on five when stumps were drawn at 5:51pm after an extended session. Shubman Gill and Co. deserve credit for their bowlers’ early blows, as they did not leave the field even when the covers were being brought on because of the dark, wet conditions a few minutes earlier.With the hosts trailing by 495 runs, India are now in control of the Test.Jurel was involved in two vital partnerships, adding 112 for the seventh wicket with Pant, which lifted India from 307 for six, and 39 for the eighth with Manav Suthar. During his stand with Pant, Jurel played the ideal foil, reaching a patient fifty off 97 balls.Like Devdutt Padikkal, Jurel has enjoyed a breakout series. Having arrived in Sri Lanka without a fifty in eight innings and under pressure from Sarfaraz Khan for the No. 6 spot, he made a crucial 51 in the first Test and now has 173 runs in two Tests at 86.50.Rishabh Pant, meanwhile, struck his 21st Test half-century and became India’s leading run-scorer in World Test Championship history, surpassing Shubman Gill. Pant now has 2,948 runs in 42 WTC Tests, ahead of Gill’s 2,917.Earlier, India resumed on 300 for five and lost debutant Saransh Jain early for six.
Article Summary: Dhruv Jurel scores 115 not out as India declare on 503-9 on Day Two of second Test in Colombo. Rishabh Pant scores 63 as Sri Lanka are reduced to 8-2 in their second innings. Sri Lanka trail by 495 runs going into the final day.

Article Title: Dhruv Jurel scripts history with Test century in Colombo, joins Hardik Pandya in rare Sri Lanka record

Dhruv Jurel's second Test century was more than just a personal milestone. The India wicketkeeper-batter also etched his name alongside Hardik Pandya in an exclusive list after producing a composed unbeaten 115 against Sri Lanka in the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo.Jurel became only the second Indian batter to score a Test century in Sri Lanka while batting at No. 7 or lower, joining Pandya, who made 108 at Pallekele in 2017. Jurel walked in at No. 7 and remained unbeaten as India declared their first innings at 503/9 on Day 2.The milestone came after a patient yet authoritative innings from the 25-year-old, who finished with nine fours and two sixes. Jurel reached his century in 171 balls and then accelerated, eventually ending unbeaten on 115 off 177 deliveries. Jurel's first Test century had come against the West Indies in Ahmedabad in October 2025, when he made 125.Jurel had reached 95 before rain brought an early end to the second session, leaving him just five runs short of three figures. When play resumed, he found himself alongside Mohammed Siraj with India's score at 475/8. The wait for the century proved more nerve-wracking than expected. Jurel remained stuck on 99 for 13 deliveries before finally taking a quick single to reach the landmark.He celebrated by hitting Asitha Fernando for a six and then added another maximum off the Sri Lankan pacer as India moved beyond the 500-run mark. Jurel's late acceleration ensured India finished with a formidable total before captain Shubman Gill called for the declaration.Jurel's century was built on important partnerships throughout the second day. The most significant came with Rishabh Pant, who returned to the crease after retiring hurt on Day 1. The pair launched an aggressive counter-attack and added 112 runs for the seventh wicket, taking India from 307/6 to 419/6 at lunch.Pant contributed 63, including six fours and two sixes, before falling shortly after lunch. Jurel then continued to shepherd the lower order, adding 39 with Manav Suthar and another useful stand with Mohammed Siraj.India declared at 503/9 after 138 overs, with Jurel unbeaten on 115 and Prasidh Krishna on four. Devdutt Padikkal had earlier scored 117, while Pant and captain Shubman Gill made half-centuries. Asitha Fernando was Sri Lanka's most successful bowler with 4/106. India then needed only three overs to make an impact with the ball.Prasidh Krishna removed Lahiru Udara for one before debutant Manav Suthar trapped nightwatchman Prabath Jayasuriya LBW for two. Sri Lanka finished the rain-hit day at 8/2, trailing by 495 runs.
Article Summary: India declared their first innings at 503/9 on Day 2 of the second Test. Dhruv Jurel was unbeaten on 115 at the end of the day. The 25-year-old became only the second Indian batter to score a Test century in Sri Lanka while batting at No. 7 or lower, joining Hardik Pandya.

Dhruv Jurel’s second Test century was as much about his roots as it was about his growing confidence with the bat.After completing a composed unbeaten 115 against Sri Lanka on a rain-hit second day, the India wicketkeeper-batter unveiled a tattoo on his left bicep carrying the words ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’, a tribute to his family and the values he grew up with.“My grandfather was a farmer and my father a soldier. He faced 177 deliveries, remained largely risk-free and helped India recover from 307 for six to post a commanding 503 for nine declared.His most important partnership came with Rishabh Pant , with the pair adding 112 runs for the seventh wicket.Pant, who had retired hurt on three after being struck during the first Test, battled through another difficult period before making 63. I always ask him what I should do in different situations,” Jurel added.Jurel eventually reached his century in 171 balls after rain had interrupted his progress on 95. Once he crossed the landmark, he accelerated, hitting Fernando for two sixes before India captain Shubman Gill declared on 503.The innings also reflected Jurel’s ability to handle interruptions, something he has become accustomed to in a rain-affected series.“I am used to the stop-start. I was looking to build partnerships,” he said.Yet despite the satisfaction of reaching three figures, Jurel was quick to keep his achievement in perspective.“When you represent India, there are butterflies. I scored 100 today but start on zero tomorrow,” he added.With India reducing Sri Lanka to 8 for two by stumps, Jurel’s hundred had put the visitors firmly in command, while his celebration offered a glimpse into the personal story behind the batter’s latest landmark.

Off the pads and away it went in a flash for a boundary. The two fielders positioned at deep mid-wicket and long-on were mere spectators as Dhruv Jurel moved to 95, within striking distance of a well-deserved hundred. There was a slight delay for the right-hander as the ground staff rushed in with the big covers. However, the match resumed and when the moment finally happened, relief was written all over the youngster's face as he took off his helmet.Jurel took his sweet time getting from 99 to three figures, and the 100th run was almost suicidal as he just hit and ran for his life. The fielder at mid-off collected cleanly but couldn't hit the stumps. A diving Jurel reached the magical number, stood up, soaked in the moment and celebrated with his overjoyed partner Mohammed Siraj, who played his part by holding up one end.There were so many storylines for this series, but Jurel's was the most important. Not Devdutt Padikkal at No. 3 and not Manav Suthar as the finger spinner, but Jurel as the specialist batter, and whether he had it in him to retain his spot for the remainder of the cycle.The Indian team management has been mighty impressed with his work ethic and technique but was running out of patience with his inability to make meaningful contributions.After the whitewash against South Africa, where he scored only 29 runs in four innings, the pressure mounted further, and the message conveyed was, "time to show that you are more than just a wicketkeeper-batter". The think tank backed him ahead of other specialist options for a spot in the Playing XI because of what they saw in the nets and on shadow tours. However, when this didn't translate into consistency in Indian whites, his clock was set on borrowed time.In more ways than one, this was a make-or-break series for Jurel. Sarfaraz Khan was breathing down his neck, and the time was right to make his India A exposure in Galle count. Jurel didn't have the most ideal outing in the warm-up fixture in Colombo. He looked far from comfortable in the nets and during match simulations. However, come match day, he turned the switch on and contributed with a crucial 51-run knock lower down the order.The confidence from his Test runs showed in the only net session he had in Colombo, as he comfortably dealt with spin and launched plenty into the stands while batting alongside the likes of Rishabh Pant and Shubman Gill. His movements looked far more assured and the connections sounded sweeter.Day 1 and Day 2 at the Sinhalese Sports Club (SSC) ground were an extension of the fun he was having near the centre wicket two days before the Test, but the relentlessness of the Sri Lankan quicks forced him to grind out a hundred he will remember for a very long time. He started the repair job with Ravindra Jadeja before the left-hander started facing discomfort in his wrist and was eventually dismissed for 43 on the opening day. Then came debutant Saransh Jain, and the immediate goal was to survive the remainder and ensure there were no further casualties heading into the second day.The goal was accomplished, but the suspense surrounding Rishabh Pant, who took a blow on his wrist, left a mixed feeling before normalcy returned on the second day. Saransh was dismissed early, and Pant walked in to join Jurel in the middle. The two wicketkeepers, with their contrasting styles of play, survived the early pressure. Once they settled in, it was a period of fluency and absolute control.India scored at nearly 4.5 an over when the two were in the middle, and they never looked to be in any urgency to press on the accelerator. Yes, it can look a bit different with Pant, but even he wasn't at his freakish best as the runs accumulated at a very healthy rate.Jurel tackled the short-ball plan with a lot of control and looked equally at ease against the spin twins Prabath Jayasuriya and Keshara Nuwantha. It was the kind of pitch that would reward patience as a batter, and Jurel definitely learned from his teammates, staying away from playing loose shots.The Indian camp invested in Jurel, allowing him time to grow and learn on the job. When impatience was growing, the wicketkeeper-batter showed why the trust in his batting abilities wasn't misplaced. Runs at No. 7 are gold dust, and the last Test hundred from No. 7 or lower for India was Nitish Kumar Reddy's 114 at the MCG in December 2024. Jurel is also only the second Indian batter after Hardik Pandya (108 at Pallekele in 2017) to score a hundred from No. 7 or lower for India in Sri Lanka.If Jurel can continue this volume, he will solve a very crucial batting piece for captain Shubman Gill and coach Gautam Gambhir.
Article Summary: India's Dhruv Jurel scored a crucial 51-run knock lower down the order. The right-hander took his sweet time getting from 99 to three figures. The 100th run was almost suicidal as he just hit and ran for his life.

Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Medal tally of India's athletes by birth state/UT

Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off it

Manipur still talking about 2023

Rajasthan: 14 years and counting

Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy picture

And then come Tamil Nadu and others

The ones somewhere in the middle

How active are states/UTs with CWG medallists in promoting sport

Does it matter so much?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch

Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.

Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.
